domain:
Process Description – Care Allowance

The citizen begins by starting application.  Then the citizen needs to submit the information, including the child's age, medical certificate from the specialist and the number of caregivers. Once all information is submitted, the system robots must determine the fact: it must determine whether the age is minor, it must verify the certificate using the verification system, and it must check the child's national insurance membership. All of the above steps needs to be done once.
Based on the robots precheck, the following  rejection consequences are produced:
	• If the certificate is fake, the caseworker must reject it and must not approve it.
	• If the child doesn't have the national insurance membership, the caseworker must reject it and must not approve it.


Once the robot's precheck are passed, the caseworker must manually assess the criteria.

If the child is adult:
	• The caseworker will assess whether the child has developmental disability
	• The caseworker will assess whether the child need continuous supervision (life-threatening case) and care

Otherwise:
	• The caseworker must assess whether the child has illness or disability
	• The caseworker must assess whether the child needs continuous supervision

Moreover, 
	• The caseworker needs to determine whether care requires caregiver absent from work
	• If the citizen input number of caregiver more than 1 during submission, the caseworker must determine whether the care needs justifies a second caregivers.


Once all of the manual assessment is done, if any of the applicable conditions fails, the caseworker will reject it. Otherwise, the caseworker will grant the care allowance.
Additionally, during assessing the criteria, the caseworker must open a case after the robot precheck finishes. After the caseworker open the case, can assess criteria can happen.
Moreover, after the caseworker opened case, he can ask for both similar cases and relevant law. Then the system robot must find the similar cases or relevant laws. Once the finding is complete, the caseworker must review the similar cases or review relevant laws.
During reviewing information of both similar cases or relevant law, the manually assessing the information is blocked until the review is finished. And it also blocks the grant decision as well. 
When grant decision is finished,  the robot must summarize the case and the caseworker must issues assessment and justification after the robot summarization. Until then, the citizen can see the justification after issuing.

entries.text: start to propose some entities and roles

Suggested roles and entities:

**Roles** (actors)
- Citizen: starts the application and submits the information.
- Caseworker: opens the case, assesses, rejects or grants, and issues the justification.
- Robot: the system robot that does the precheck, finds similar cases and law, and summarizes the case.
- Verification System: the external system that verifies the medical certificate.

**Entities** (data containers with a lifecycle)
- Application: the care allowance application, with the child's age, number of caregivers and the decision.
- Medical Certificate: submitted by the citizen and verified.
- Case: opened by the caseworker, holds the assessments, the research and the summary.
- Similar Cases and Relevant Law: the information that is found and then reviewed. I'd model these as two separate entities because they are requested and reviewed separately.

Shall I add these roles and entities to the document?

options.label: Add them
options.message: Yes, add these roles and entities to the document.

entries.text: Sounds good, but I think medical certificate & case & rele... are too detailed, skip those

The plan adds the four roles and one entity, and the check finds no problems. I left out Medical Certificate, Case, Similar Cases and Relevant Law, as you asked.

- **Roles:** Citizen, Caseworker, Robot and Verification System.
- **Entity:** Application. The case-related actions can sit on it later.

Please approve or reject the plan with the buttons.

The document now has the roles Citizen, Caseworker, Robot and Verification System, and the entity Application. The check reports no problems.

Next I suggest the actions for the first stage of the process, the application and the robot precheck:
- Citizen starts application.
- Citizen submits information, with inputs for the child's age, the medical certificate and the number of caregivers.
- Robot determines minor.
- Robot verifies certificate, using the Verification System.
- Robot checks national insurance membership.

Shall I add these actions to the document?

entries.text: Yes, add these actions to the document.

The plan adds five actions to the Application entity, each with an action specification. The check finds no problems.

- **start application:** initiated by Citizen.
- **submit information:** initiated by Citizen. Its inputs are child age (int), medical certificate (string) and caregiver count (int).
- **determine minor:** initiated by Robot. Its output is minor result (boolean).
- **verify certificate:** initiated by Robot and observed by Verification System. Its output is certificate valid (boolean).
- **check national insurance membership:** initiated by Robot. Its output is membership found (boolean).

Input and output names can't contain keywords such as "of" or "is". So I used "caregiver count" and "minor result" instead of "number of caregivers" and "is minor".

Please approve or reject the plan with the buttons.

entries.text:
The five actions and their specifications are now in the document, and the check reports no problems.

Next I suggest the second batch of actions, covering the rejection and the case opening:
- Caseworker rejects application.
- Caseworker approves application. The text says the caseworker "must not approve" a fake or uninsured case, so this action is needed to model that.
- Caseworker opens case.
- Caseworker assesses criteria. Splitting this by adult or minor can come later, in the enabled specifications.

Shall I add these actions to the document?

options.label: Add second batch
options.message: Yes, add the second batch of actions.

entries.text: I think assess criteira is too general, other look good

Agreed. "Assess criteria" is really several separate assessments, so I'd replace it with specific actions:

- Assess developmental disability (adult child)
- Assess continuous supervision with life-threatening risk (adult child)
- Assess illness or disability (minor child)
- Assess continuous supervision (minor child)
- Assess caregiver absence from work
- Assess second caregiver need (when there is more than one caregiver)

Together with the earlier ones, the batch would be:
- Caseworker rejects application.
- Caseworker approves application.
- Caseworker opens case.
- The six assessments above, each initiated by the Caseworker. Each would have a boolean output for its result.

That is 9 actions. Shall I add these actions to the document?

options.label: Add these actions
options.message: Yes, add these actions to the document.

entries.text: Yes, add these actions to the document.

The plan adds nine actions to the Application entity, each with an action specification. The check finds no problems.

All nine are initiated by the Caseworker:
- **reject application, approve application and open case:** no inputs or outputs.
- **Six assessments:** assess developmental disability, assess life threatening supervision, assess illness disability, assess continuous supervision, assess caregiver absence and assess second caregiver need. Each has a boolean output called "assessment result".

I shortened two names to "assess life threatening supervision" and "assess illness disability". Please approve or reject the plan with the buttons.

entries.reason: I prefer assess to have the assess option as input

entries.text:
I'm not sure what you mean by "assess option as input". I see two readings:

1. **One generic action:** a single "assess criteria" action with an input such as `criterion` (string). Its value would say which criterion is assessed, for example developmental disability or second caregiver need. The result would be a boolean output.
2. **Six specific actions:** these stay, and each takes an input, such as `option` (boolean), that the caseworker sets to record the outcome. This replaces the output I proposed.

Which one do you want? In either case, reject application, approve application and open case stay as before.

options.label: One generic action
options.message: I want one generic assess criteria action with a criterion input.

options.label: Six specific actions
options.message: Keep the six specific actions, each with an option input instead of an output.

entries.text: I mean assess xxx should have the caseworker 's opiopn yes or no as input

The revised plan adds nine actions to the Application entity, each with an action specification. The check finds no problems.

All nine are initiated by the Caseworker:
- **reject application, approve application and open case:** no inputs or outputs.
- **Six assessments:** assess developmental disability, assess life threatening supervision, assess illness disability, assess continuous supervision, assess caregiver absence and assess second caregiver need. Each now takes the caseworker's yes or no as a boolean input called "opinion". None has an output.

Please approve or reject the plan with the buttons.

The nine actions and their specifications are now in the document, and the check reports no problems.

Next I suggest the last batch of actions, covering the research and the closing steps:
- Caseworker asks for similar cases.
- Caseworker asks for relevant law.
- Robot finds similar cases.
- Robot finds relevant law.
- Caseworker reviews similar cases.
- Caseworker reviews relevant law.
- Robot summarizes case.
- Caseworker issues assessment and justification.
- Citizen views justification.

Shall I add these actions to the document?

options.label: Add these actions
options.message: Yes, add these actions to the document.

entries.text: Yes, add these actions to the document.

The plan adds the last nine actions to the Application entity, each with an action specification. The check finds no problems.

- **Caseworker:** ask for similar cases, ask for relevant law, review similar cases and review relevant law. Issue assessment and justification is also initiated by the Caseworker, and the Citizen observes it.
- **Robot:** find similar cases, find relevant law and summarize case.
- **Citizen:** view justification.

None of the nine has inputs or outputs.

Please approve or reject the plan with the buttons.

All the actions are now in the document, and the check reports no problems.

Next I suggest the data properties on Application. These hold the values that the process rules depend on:
- child age (int)
- caregiver count (int)
- is minor (boolean), set by the robot's minor check
- certificate valid (boolean)
- insurance member (boolean)
- one boolean opinion per assessment, for the final grant or reject decision

The last group is six properties, which brings the batch to 11. I'd start with the first five and add the six assessment opinions in the next batch.

Shall I add these five data properties to the document?

options.label: Add the five properties
options.message: Yes, add the first five data properties to the document.

options.label: Add all eleven
options.message: Add all eleven data properties in one batch.

entries.text: but I think, is minor is computation, and certificate valid is likewise, I would like a data container containing the data, not those ones

Understood. The Application entity is the data container, and it should hold only the submitted data. The computed results (minor, certificate valid, insurance membership) come from the robot's actions, so they shouldn't be stored as properties.

Proposed data properties on Application:
- child age (int)
- medical certificate (string)
- caregiver count (int)

The "more than one caregiver" rule can then be checked against caregiver count. The assessment opinions can wait until we reach the specifications.

Shall I add these three data properties to the document?

options.label: Add these properties
options.message: Yes, add these three data properties to the document.

entries.text: Yes, add these three data properties to the document.

The plan adds three data properties to the Application entity, and the check finds no problems.

- **child age:** int
- **medical certificate:** string
- **caregiver count:** int

I did not add the computed results (minor, certificate valid, insurance membership) as properties.

Please approve or reject the plan with the buttons.

The three data properties are now on Application, and the check reports no problems.

Next I suggest the states of Application. These are the lifecycle stages the text mentions:
- **started:** the application has been started.
- **submitted:** the information has been submitted.
- **prechecked:** the robot's three checks are done.
- **case opened:** the caseworker has opened the case.
- **rejected:** the caseworker has rejected it.
- **granted:** the caseworker has approved it.

Each state needs a state specification, and I'd add those in the same batch.

Shall I add these states to the document?

options.label: Add the states
options.message: Yes, add these states to the document.

entries.text: Yes, add these states to the document.

The plan adds six states to Application, each with a state specification. The check finds no problems.

Each state is defined by the action that was executed:
- **started:** start application was executed.
- **submitted:** submit information was executed.
- **prechecked:** determine minor, verify certificate and check national insurance membership were all executed.
- **case opened:** open case was executed.
- **rejected:** reject application was executed.
- **granted:** approve application was executed.

Please approve or reject the plan with the buttons.
